items.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I didn’t work with any groups except I went with Johnny Hammond Smith’s for about two years.

ctx.x: And you started almost from the beginning having your own band.
Yeah. I didn’t work with any groups except I went with Johnny Hammond Smith’s for about two years. And that was it. So I didn’t have any — there was nothing visual.
Nobody knew who I was. And I just stuck it out. But if you get a wife, four girls to feed and a mortgage, you’ll find a way. That’s what happened.

items.title: Houston Person Part 1 interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995…
items.q: Oh, boy, I’ve worked with them all. Charlie Earland, Jack McDuff, Sonny Phillips, Joey DeFrancesco, oh boy, Groove Holmes, Johnny Hammond Smith.

ctx.x: Tell us about some of the great organ players you’ve worked with.

Oh, boy, I’ve worked with them all. Charlie Earland, Jack McDuff, Sonny Phillips, Joey DeFrancesco, oh boy, Groove Holmes, Johnny Hammond Smith. Yeah. I’ve worked with a lot of organ players, and they were all good. They were the greatest. I also worked with Jimmy Smith, who is the king, so I worked with a lot of them.

What’s it been like visiting different parts of the country and other countries, have you done a lot of traveling and do you notice a difference in how people relate to your particular brand of music?
